title: Deciphering the tomato phosphate starvation response: Functional and transcriptional roles of SlPHR3 and SlPHR4
content: Phosphorus (P) is an essential nutrient for plants, primarily taken up from the soil in the form of inorganic phosphate (Pi) (Paz-Ares et al. 2022). However, the fraction of soluble Pi available to roots represents only a small portion of the total phosphorus in the soil (Holford 1997; Prathap et al. 2022). Pi is relatively immobile due to its strong adsorption to soil particles and its tendency to form insoluble complexes with calcium, iron, and aluminum oxides or hydroxides, processes that are highly influenced by soil composition and pH (Poirier et al. 2022). The low mobility of Pi in soil poses a significant challenge for plant productivity (Bucher 2006).
